title: Functions, keywords, closures and argument sharing
outcome: Write reusable functions with explicit contracts and distinguish local rebinding from mutation of a passed object.

exercises.title: Use defaults
exercises.answer: A default is part of the function contract and should be recorded when it matters scientifically.

exercises.title: Override one choice
exercises.answer: Explicit keyword configuration makes a transformation reproducible.

exercises.title: Build a closure
exercises.task: Create a scale 3 function and apply it to 2.
exercises.hint: The returned function retains its scale binding.
exercises.answer: A closure packages a transformation and context; it does not necessarily copy mutable captured objects.

exercises.title: Trace a rebound argument
exercises.task: Call rebind on a caller array.
exercises.hint: The local name is assigned another array.
exercises.answer: Rebinding the argument name is different from mutating the shared object.

exercises.title: Trace a mutated argument
exercises.task: Call change_first! on a nonempty vector.
exercises.expected: Its first element becomes 99 and the returned object aliases it.
exercises.hint: Compare identity as well as contents.
exercises.answer: The naming convention warns callers that the operation changes shared state.

exercises.title: Reject an empty mutation
exercises.task: Call change_first! on an empty vector.
exercises.answer: A clear input contract produces a more useful diagnostic than an accidental indexing failure.
